grades.quote: The paging hardware translates a virtual address by using the top 27 bits of the 39 bits to index into the page table to find a PTE
grades.reason: xv6 text on Sv39: 39-bit VA, a 27-bit index into the page table, and a 12-bit offset. It does not cover the 9-bit-per-level split or the walk loop, so it is only a partial basis for the correspondence.
Covers Sv48, not Sv39 field layout or the xv6 walk loop. It only says Sv48 adds a level on top of Sv39.

grades.quote: The 27-bit VPN is translated into a 44-bit PPN via a three-level page table, while the 12-bit page offset is untranslated.
grades.reason: The RISC-V spec's Sv39 VA format: VPN[2], VPN[1] and VPN[0] of 9 bits each plus a 12-bit offset, translated through a three-level page table. This gives the field side of the correspondence, but it has no xv6 walk loop.
